subject: Latency guardrail variance request — BetaEmbed v2 launch
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@fluxhealth.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Latency guardrail variance request — BetaEmbed v2 launch

Hi Samir,

Appreciate the momentum getting BetaEmbed v2 integrated into FluxHealth's ingestion pipeline. As discussed on the call, the model variant we plan to ship in "preview" has a few known latency trade-offs at peak concurrency. Because your integration will hit bursts of large batched requests during nightly processing windows, we need a short-term variance from our standard latency guardrails while we complete the final optimizations.

Request summary: we propose a 4-week SLA variance for the BetaEmbed v2 route starting on the planned go-live date (see dates below). During the variance period Redwood will:
- Accept a temporary relaxation at the p95 token-latency target from 120ms to 280ms for high-concurrency windows (midnight–04:00 PT).
- Provide a guaranteed fallback to BetaEmbed-quant (quantized variant) when p99 queue depth exceeds a threshold (automatic).
- Deliver a daily latency profile CSV and a dashboard share to FluxHealth's procurement and SRE.

Attachments: I attached the formal SLO exception form and the latency profile snapshot our engineering team generated from the internal canary.

Ask: please confirm FluxHealth's acceptance of the variance and any required wording your legal or procurement team needs in the amendment. If acceptable we will prepare a short DocuSign amendment to the MSA and lock the monitoring hooks with Laura's team.

Planned schedule:
- Proposed go-live (canary window): 2026-11-15
- Full production traffic: 2026-11-18 (subject to canary metrics)
- Variance end date: 2026-12-15

Next step: Samir — can your procurement lead confirm the timeline and whether a statement of work or schedule is sufficient for you?

Thanks,

Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0196

Attachment: slo-exception-form.pdf (application/pdf)
Attachment: betaembed-v2-latency-profiles.csv (text/csv)

From: Samir Shah <samir@fluxhealth.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@fluxhealth.ai
Date: 2026-11-08T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Latency guardrail variance request — BetaEmbed v2 launch

Neha — thanks for the clear write-up. A few quick clarifying items from our side before we escalate to procurement/legal: 

1) Fallback behavior — when Redwood flips to BetaEmbed-quant, will there be any functional differences in embedding vectors (versioning) we should expect? We need assurances that embeddings will remain compatible or that you will provide mapping/translation guidance.

2) SLA credits — procurement will ask whether there's any compensation mechanism if we see repeated breaches beyond the variance window. We don't expect it, but they want the option captured.

3) Observability — can you guarantee a push of alerts to our existing PagerDuty/Splunk integration? The daily CSV is fine but we also need real-time paging for sustained degradation.

If we can get explicit answers for those three items, I can route to procurement and aim to come back with a signed amendment in 48–72 hours.

— Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Platform Integrations, FluxHealth
samir@fluxhealth.ai

On a separate note — we plan a large batch ingest on 11/20, so if the variance overlaps that date we will want to coordinate a smaller test earlier in the week.

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@fluxhealth.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-08T13:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Latency guardrail variance request — BetaEmbed v2 launch

Samir / Neha — quick technical clarifications from the product team: 

1) Embedding compatibility: BetaEmbed v2 and the quantized variant (BetaEmbed-quant) produce vectors from the same model family with a documented 32-bit -> 8-bit quantization mapping. For typical cosine-similarity retrieval we expect <1.5% delta in top-k recall at k=10 in our internal tests. We'll provide a short mapping note and a deterministic post-processing script if you need exact reproduction.

2) Fallback semantics: fallback is deterministic and happens at the request-router level when queue depth or p99 latency crosses thresholds. We will add a header x-redwood-model-variant to responses so you can detect which variant served the request and backfill reindexing where needed.

3) SLA credits: Redwood's standard SLA credits apply post-variance window. During the agreed variance window we propose no automatic credits; however, if there are sustained degradations beyond 3 consecutive days above the variance threshold we will offer a one-time service credit pro-rated for that period. We can include the exact credit language in the amendment.

4) Observability: we will enable a streaming alert integration to your PagerDuty project and push an HTTP webhook to your Splunk endpoint for degraded windows. Laura — can you confirm retention settings and whether we need to provision any additional API keys for FluxHealth?

I'll attach the latency profile CSV from the most recent internal canary. The CSV shows p50/p95/p99 across the traffic shapes you described.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Product Engineer, Serving Runtime
dev.patel@redwood.ai

Attachment: betaembed-v2-latency-profiles.csv (text/csv)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@fluxhealth.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Latency guardrail variance request — BetaEmbed v2 launch

Samir / team — operational notes and confirmation from SRE: 

- Monitoring: Redwood will create a per-route dashboard and a PagerDuty service tied to FluxHealth's integration. We will emit the following signals: p50/p95/p99 token-latency, queue depth, error-rate (5xx), and variant switch events (BetaEmbed-v2 -> BetaEmbed-quant).
- Retention & logs: We'll retain trace-level logs for 30 days for the variance period and make a secure link available to FluxHealth security for audit requests.
- Circuit breaker policy: If queue depth reaches the safety limit for >10s, the router will reject new requests with a 429 and return a JSON payload with suggested retry-after. We will also expose a 'grace' window toggle for your team to pause operation during your large batch ingest on 11/20.
- Approval: From an operations standpoint Laura approves the 4-week variance window provided the fallback header and PagerDuty hook are in place before canary.

I'll coordinate keys with your security/procurement contact — procurement@fluxhealth.ai — to provision the webhook. Please confirm required encryption or IP allow-listing if needed.

Regards,

Laura Bennett
Head of SRE, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: (none)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@fluxhealth.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@fluxhealth.ai
Date: 2026-11-09T17:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Latency guardrail variance request — BetaEmbed v2 launch

Samir — great, thanks for the quick review. Below are the action items and next steps so procurement has a single doc to review: 

Action items:
- Redwood to add explicit amendment language covering the variance window, fallback behavior, credit language for sustained breaches, and the PagerDuty/Splunk webhook terms (we will draft). (Owner: Neha / Legal)
- Dev to supply the mapping script and ensure x-redwood-model-variant header is present in canary traffic. (Owner: Dev)
- Laura to provision the PagerDuty service and confirm webhook endpoints; coordinate key exchange with procurement. (Owner: Laura)

Timeline:
- Redwood to circulate DocuSign amendment by 2026-11-11 (goal)
- FluxHealth to sign by 2026-11-13 to meet the 11/15 canary date

If procurement is happy with the pager/integration and the credit language, we will consider this approved on your side. I'll circulate the amendment and a one-page appendix summarizing the technical fallbacks.

Please let me know if FluxHealth requires this variance to be captured in a separate SOW; otherwise we'll issue a short schedule to the MSA.

Thanks — looking forward to the canary.

Neha Kapoor
